A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same LAMP research work. Their complete 33-page contents, including figures, equations, tables, and appendices, are readable and support reliable matching across relocation and renumbering.

before.justification: v2 reports original generation, extrapolation, optimization, and ablation results on DrivAerNet++ and BlendedNet, plus appendix experiments and human-annotated safety validation.

after.justification: v3 retains these original results and adds vehicle-family comparisons, runtime figures, and safety-filter acceptance rates.

M1.justification: Shared-initialization SDF fitting, parameter-constrained affine mixing, decoding, and the safety metric remain unchanged. The non-implicit decoder experiment and regularized multi-objective formulation already appear in v2's appendices.

E1.justification: v3 adds evaluated Toyota Supra, Toyota C-HR, and Porsche Carrera GT families, substantially broadening vehicle geometry coverage to sports cars, SUVs, and convertibles. DrivAerNet++, BlendedNet, and the plate-with-hole study are retained; BlendedNet is not newly added.

E2.justification: Conditioned 3DShape2VecSet joins DNI and AE-LPA in the new vehicle comparison, Table 4. Original experiments retain their comparator sets. Table 11 also introduces a runtime comparison with LION, although it does not establish a matched experimental rerun.

E3.justification: The added vehicle study uses 50 samples per family and evaluates ramp angle, diffuser angle, length, width, and greenhouse angle through direct mesh measurements. Existing benchmark splits, extrapolation sweeps, and metrics remain unchanged; the new study's complete testing and measurement procedures are not specified.

E4.justification: New Appendix L analyzes how often generations from the reported experiments pass the safety filter, complementing the existing diagnostic and extrapolation-volume analyses. Appendix I adds a compute-cost comparison. The initialization ablation in v3 Table 6 repeats results already present in v2 Appendix F.

E5.justification: Appendix F retains the same seed comparison and reporting practice. No repeated-run counts, confidence intervals, significance tests, or uncertainty-estimation procedures are added. The new validity percentages are outcomes, not uncertainty estimates.

E6.justification: v3 adds substantial cross-vehicle results in Table 4, including LAMP R2 values of 0.97, 0.99, and 0.93, plus runtime figures in Table 11 and safety-filter pass rates of 84–98% in Table 12. Original benchmark and appendix scores are retained; these additions are not same-setting performance improvements.

T1.justification: The assumptions, theorem, and proofs in Section 3 and Appendices A–C are unchanged. The regularized mixing objective and extrapolation-volume derivation also match after appendix renumbering.

C1.justification: The abstract changes the claimed minimum sample requirement from 100 to 50, and the introduction expands the application claim to additional vehicle families. The central affine-mixing contribution and extrapolation claim of up to 100% beyond training ranges remain.

C2.justification: v3 explicitly positions LAMP as candidate generation preceding CFD and engineering validation, interprets the new vehicle results as broader applicability, and explains lower filter acceptance under simultaneous constraints. Appendix J repeats existing limitations rather than adding the advertised extended discussion.

D1.justification: v3 adds a code-access link and reports preprocessing and inference costs, including approximately five minutes per exemplar. Appendix L newly clarifies that headline quantitative results are reported before safety filtering; this disclosure does not establish a changed evaluation procedure.

R1.justification: v3 adds references covering newer generators, neural representations, model merging, and CAD, including 3DShape2VecSet, CLAY, GETMesh, and CAD-Recode. The related-work organization and positioning against HyperDiffusion, latent traversal, and earlier weight interpolation remain substantially unchanged.

P1.justification: Rewriting concentrates on the abstract and introduction. v3 adds transfer and runtime passages, makes limitations unnumbered, adds impact and acknowledgment statements, and removes the LLM-writing disclosure. Most method, original experimental, and appendix prose remains unchanged.

P2.justification: v3 adopts a two-column conference layout for the main text and substantially resizes and relocates existing displays. It adds a vehicle figure, vehicle/runtime/validity tables, and a partial redisplay of the initialization table. All original figure graphics are retained.

improvement.justification: Direct geometric evaluation across three additional vehicle families strengthens evidence beyond v2's largely surrogate-based validation. Appendix L makes reliability more assessable by disclosing unfiltered results and actual filter acceptance rates. These gains are useful but bounded: new measurement and baseline implementation details remain sparse, and Table 11 does not establish comparable end-to-end runtime costs.
